title: Your weight on other planets
examples: Does gravity affect things on Earth too?
If I weigh less on the Moon, does my mass change?
Which planet has the strongest gravity?

explain.say: Gravity is a force that pulls things towards each other. Everything with mass has gravity.
Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: the solar system. Look at the sun, the mercury and the venus. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
Your weight is how hard gravity pulls on your mass. It changes depending on where you are.
The Moon has much less gravity than Earth. You would weigh about one sixth here.
Jupiter is a very big planet with strong gravity. You would weigh about two and a half times more.
If you weighed 60 kilograms on Earth, you would weigh about 10 kilograms on the Moon.
When you are at the beach, the Moon's gravity pulls you gently. It is always pulling you towards it.

faq.q: Does my mass change when I go to another planet?
faq.a: No, your mass stays the same no matter where you are. Mass is the amount of stuff you are made of.

faq.q: Is gravity the same everywhere in space?
faq.a: No, gravity changes depending on the size and mass of the object you are near. Bigger objects pull harder.
asks: Does gravity get weaker far away?
What affects the strength of gravity?

faq.q: Why is Jupiter's gravity so much stronger than Earth's?
faq.a: Jupiter is a very large planet with a huge amount of mass. More mass means a stronger pull of gravity.
asks: What makes Jupiter's gravity so strong?

faq.q: If I jump on the Moon, will I go higher than on Earth?
faq.a: Yes, because the Moon's gravity is weaker, you will feel lighter and jump higher. You will still come back down though.
asks: Will I jump higher on the Moon?
How does low gravity affect jumping?

faq.q: What is the difference between weight and mass?
faq.a: Mass is the amount of matter in you, measured in kilograms. Weight is the force of gravity pulling on that mass, measured in Newtons.
asks: Are weight and mass the same thing?
What unit do I use for weight?

facts: Gravity is a natural force that pulls objects with mass together.
Weight is the measure of the gravitational force on an object.
The Moon has significantly less gravity than Earth.
Jupiter has a much greater mass than Earth, resulting in stronger gravity.

quiz.say: If your mass is 50 kilograms, what is your approximate weight on the Moon?
quiz.why: The Moon's gravity is about one sixth of Earth's, so you divide your Earth weight by six.

wrong.0: Newtons measure force, but you must account for the Moon's weaker pull.
wrong.1: This number relates to Jupiter, not the Moon's weaker pull.
wrong.3: This is your mass, not your weight. Mass does not change with gravity.

quiz.say: If you weighed 100 Newtons on Earth, what would your weight be on Jupiter?
quiz.why: Jupiter's gravity is about two and a half times stronger than Earth's, so you multiply your Earth weight by 2.5.

wrong.0: This calculation suggests gravity is weaker, which is incorrect for Jupiter.
wrong.1: This is too small; you must multiply by 2.5, not divide.
wrong.3: You cannot ignore the difference in gravity between the two planets.

quiz.say: If you weigh 150 Newtons on Earth, what is your weight on the Moon?
quiz.why: You must calculate one sixth of your Earth weight to find your weight on the Moon.

wrong.0: This forgets that the Moon's gravity is much weaker than Earth's.
wrong.1: Weight changes by division, not by adding a fixed number.
wrong.2: While dividing is right, you must use the specific fraction for the Moon, which is one sixth.
